subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Solving equations graphically and analytically

points.text: Choosing an analytic or a graphical method
Using technology when no algebraic method exists
Applying graphs and equations to real contexts

bigPicture: Choose the method: algebra when an exact answer exists and is asked for (Paper 1); the GDC when no algebraic method exists or a decimal is fine (Paper 2).

keyIdeas.answer: When the question says 'exact', 'show that', or it is Paper 1.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you solve e^x = 3 − x?
keyIdeas.answer: No algebraic method: GDC intersection of y = e^x and y = 3 − x (x ≈ 0.792).

keyIdeas.cue: What extra step does a context need?
keyIdeas.answer: Check solutions fit the domain/context and answer in the units asked.

keyTerms.def: by plotting, usually with the GDC

misconceptions.right: x² = 2^x also has a negative root.

practice.prompt: Solve ln x = 4 − x² for x > 0.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: Which GDC feature finds intersections, and which finds zeros?

syllabusFlags: Skill spans every unit; ISL placement is an assumption.
